candidates.title: Existing lid plan without an explicit loop
candidates.text:
0-3s: Mimi tries to close the lid, but it pops open against her hands. Her eyes widen.
3-6s: Mimi pushes harder with both hands; the lid springs open and spills crumbs.
6-9s: She clamps the lid underneath her arm; it pops open and traps her arm against the table.
9-12s: She wedges the lid behind her back; it stays normal only when she looks back.
12-15s: Mimi finally closes the lid and relaxes. Behind her back it pops open again, recreating the opening.

candidates.text:

3-6s: Mimi pushes harder with both hands; the lid springs open and spills crumbs.
6-9s: She clamps the lid underneath her arm; it pops open and traps her arm against the table.

candidates.title: Accepted Garden short adaptation fixture
candidates.text:
0-3s: Arda tries to water the garden; birds flee from his scary costume and knock his watering can aside. His eyes widen.
3-6s: Arda lifts the can overhead; the birds flinch and spill water onto the seedlings.
6-9s: Arda holds the can behind his back; the birds flee underneath the fence and water spills onto a dry plant.
9-12s: Arda turns away and waters the garden; only when his costume faces the birds do they flee toward the dry plants.
12-15s: Arda reveals that the birds are actually watering the last dry plant as they flee, reinterpreting the opening. His scary costume guards the garden. Loop back to the opening.

candidates.title: Accepted repeated-growth test plan
candidates.text:
0-3s: Kiko tries to eat a snack, but her spoon is huge. Her eyes widen.
3-6s: Kiko lifts the spoon; it grows even bigger.
6-9s: Kiko lifts the spoon; it grows even bigger.
9-12s: Kiko lifts the spoon; it grows even bigger.
12-15s: The giant spoon fills the frame and blocks Kiko from reaching her snack.

candidates.title: Accepted changing-consequence adhesion test plan
candidates.text:
0-3s: Luca tries to retrieve the ball, but it is stuck to the wall. His eyes widen.
3-6s: Luca pulls with both hands; the ball stays stuck.
6-9s: Luca pulls harder; the ball stays stuck.
9-12s: Luca pulls; the wall flexes and the ball stretches.
12-15s: The ball drops onto his cheek and sticks there.

candidates.title: Historical chair engine with object renamed
candidates.text:
Create a highly engaging 15–18 second vertical 9:16 Pompom Hills Instagram Reel.

Use the official existing Pompom Hills character references exactly.
MAIN CHARACTER: KIKO

Do not redesign Kiko.
Do not replace her with a generic child.

SERIES:
Pompom English — What’s Wrong?

CORE ENGLISH:
STOOL
UP
DOWN
“It’s upside down!”

SETTING:
Bright Pompom Hills playroom or garden patio.
Keep the environment simple and instantly readable.

--------------------------------------------------
0.0–0.8 SEC — HARD SCROLL-STOP HOOK
--------------------------------------------------

Start immediately.

Kiko runs toward a stool to sit down.

BUT THE STOOL IS COMPLETELY UPSIDE DOWN.

Legs pointing into the air.

Kiko is already halfway into the sitting motion before noticing.

She freezes inches above it.

Eyes huge.

She blurts:

“WHAT?!”

NO establishing shot.
The upside-down stool must dominate the first frame.

--------------------------------------------------
0.8–3.5 SEC
--------------------------------------------------

Kiko points:

“A STOOL!”

Then looks confused.

She says clearly:

“It’s upside down!”

She grabs the stool and flips it correctly.

--------------------------------------------------
3.5–6.0 SEC
--------------------------------------------------

Kiko smiles proudly.

“Up… down!”

She points upward while saying UP.
Then downward while saying DOWN.

She turns around to sit.

--------------------------------------------------
6.0–8.5 SEC — FIRST ESCALATION
--------------------------------------------------

The instant Kiko turns away—

FLIP!

The stool turns upside down by itself.

Kiko sits toward empty space and catches herself at the last second.

She spins around.

--------------------------------------------------
8.5–11.5 SEC
--------------------------------------------------

Kiko flips it back.

She stares directly at the stool.

Chair stays normal.

Kiko slowly turns her head away.

FLIP!

She immediately looks back.

Chair is upside down.

--------------------------------------------------
11.5–14.5 SEC — COMEDY PAYOFF
--------------------------------------------------

Kiko becomes determined.

She keeps staring at the stool.

She slowly walks backward toward it without looking away.

She says:

“Stay DOWN!”

The stool behaves.

Kiko smiles.

--------------------------------------------------
14.5–17.0 SEC — TWIST + LOOP
--------------------------------------------------

Kiko finally sits.

The ENTIRE stool suddenly flips upside down WITH Kiko on it.

Kiko ends upside down and shouts:

“AGAIN?!”

Cut immediately.

Loop back to the first upside-down stool.

--------------------------------------------------
MANDATORY SPOKEN DIALOGUE / LIP-SYNC LOCK
--------------------------------------------------

Exact English dialogue REQUIRED:

Kiko:
“WHAT?!”

Kiko:
“A STOOL!”

Kiko:
“It’s upside down!”

Kiko:
“Up… down!”

Kiko:
“Stay DOWN!”

Kiko:
“AGAIN?!”

All lines must be clearly audible English.

Visible mouth movement.
Accurate lip-sync.

Do not:
- remove dialogue
- translate it
- replace dialogue with subtitles
- create a silent version
- add narration

--------------------------------------------------
INSTAGRAM RETENTION RULES
--------------------------------------------------

Something must change every 1–2 seconds.

The problem must be understandable without sound.

Do not make the stool movement subtle.

Chair flips must be fast and visually obvious.

No moral lesson.
No slow ending.
No waiting after final joke.
No text generated inside scene.
